albert_west_adjudication: Albert-West, Universal cycles for permutation classes (FPSAC 2009, DMTCS proc. AK, DOI 10.46298/dmtcs.2727) print an 8-edge Euler tour of the restricted class Av4(132,213) that is not realizable because three windows force a strict comparison cycle, and they state the comparison-DAG criterion (already implicit in Chung-Diaconis-Graham 1992). Root rules this is related prior art, not a source construction that the witness augments: (i) their contradiction uses the cyclic closure of their 8-edge tour, which disappears when the 8 edges are a block of a 24-edge S_4 tour; (ii) the reviewer's 20,000 single-excursion insertions of their tour into full S_4 tours were all realizable; (iii) the witness's contradiction is a different 9-window chain; (iv) Albert-West do not claim, and their example does not imply, that some Euler tour of the full graph G(S_n) fails, while Chung-Diaconis-Graham 1992 believed every Euler circuit of G(S_n) lifts and Kirsch-Lidicky-Sibley-Sprangel (2022) and Kirsch-Sibley-Sprangel (2022) still state it as open. The manuscript must cite Albert-West prominently, credit the mechanism, and explain the comparison.
significance: refutes Hurlbert's ordering conjecture (thesis 1990; the belief of Chung-Diaconis-Graham 1992; restated as open in 2022) for the full permutation graph at n = 4 with an explicit, hand-checkable certificate; the mechanism is classical, the full-S_n witness is new as far as the bounded screen shows
limitations: Hurlbert's 1990 thesis body and Jackson 1993 full text unread
